title: Recall Quiz: Ben Jonson & The Comedy of Humours

questions.q: Ben Jonson is most famous for popularizing which dramatic genre?
questions.explanation: He created the Comedy of Humours, where characters are driven by an overarching dominant trait.

questions.q: Which of the following is a play by Ben Jonson that satirizes human greed through a protagonist who pretends to be dying?
questions.explanation: Volpone (The Fox) is a masterpiece of satire targeting greed and legacy-hunting.

questions.q: The group of poets known as the 'Cavaliers' were politically aligned with whom during the English Civil War?
questions.explanation: The Cavaliers were Royalists who supported King Charles I.

questions.q: What does the Latin phrase 'Carpe Diem', central to Cavalier poetry, translate to?
questions.explanation: Carpe Diem urges people to enjoy life while they are young.

questions.q: Which Cavalier poet wrote the famous line 'Gather ye rosebuds while ye may'?
questions.explanation: This is the opening line of Robert Herrick's 'To the Virgins, to Make Much of Time'.

questions.q: Who wrote the lines 'Stone walls do not a prison make, / Nor iron bars a cage'?
questions.explanation: Richard Lovelace wrote this in his poem 'To Althea, from Prison'.

questions.q: According to the theory of 'humours', a person's temperament is determined by the balance of:
questions.explanation: The four fluids were blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile.

questions.q: The younger poets who admired and followed Ben Jonson's classical style were known as the:
options: Sons of Ben (or Tribe of Ben)
questions.explanation: They styled themselves as the Tribe (or Sons) of Ben.
